# Brand identity

Create a coherent identity that can be applied by its intended users, with clear provenance, usage rules and tested examples. A palette, moodboard or list of adjectives is not a finished brand system. Preserve the correct brand's existing decisions and sharing boundaries.

Read [Runtime contract](references/runtime-contract.md) in a new host. Use [Discovery and direction](references/discovery-direction.md), [Identity system](references/identity-system.md), [Applications and rollout](references/applications-rollout.md), [Brand brief](assets/brand-brief.md), [Guideline template](assets/guideline-template.md) and [Acceptance](references/acceptance.md). Use the optional contrast helper only for its documented opaque-color calculation.

## Establish the assignment

Identify the brand, audience, offer, supported positioning, actual business context, channels, constraints and decision owner. Determine whether the work is a new identity, an approved refresh, an inconsistency audit or a narrow extension. Do not replace an existing identity because a new concept is easier to generate.

Read the correct brand's approved voice, assets, colors, type licenses and usage restrictions. Separate approved facts from proposals and hypotheses. Keep brands/projects distinct. Existing audience research can support direction; invented research, testimonials or performance claims cannot.

Inspect the required deliverables and available authoring capabilities. If the request is strategy/guidelines, produce that requested result without claiming original artwork exists. If actual assets are requested, create/export and inspect them through supported tools; a description of a logo is not a logo file. Tool access does not authorize buying fonts, publishing a rebrand or uploading private assets.

## Choose a direction with reasons

Use [Discovery and direction](references/discovery-direction.md). Translate the supported strategy into concrete design criteria: recognition, tone, legibility, differentiation, practical channel use and continuity where required. Propose materially different directions when a decision needs comparison, not cosmetic color swaps presented as new concepts.

Explain tradeoffs against the brief rather than arbitrary taste scores. Test the direction on representative real applications early enough to reveal problems. Approval of a direction does not automatically approve unseen final assets or a public rollout. Preserve the exact reviewed version and any required decision path.

## Build a usable identity system

Read [Identity system](references/identity-system.md). Develop the mark/wordmark structure, approved variants, color roles, typography hierarchy, imagery/icon language, layout principles and voice/tone guidance appropriate to the assignment. Each rule should change a practical application decision; avoid generic adjectives that cannot be acted on.

For marks, inspect recognizability, silhouette, spacing, small-size behavior and one-color/reversed use at the intended sizes. Do not invent a universal minimum size or clear-space formula unrelated to the actual asset. Document measured recommendations and limits. Search or legal review may be needed for ownership questions; do not claim trademark clearance from visual novelty.

For color, define permitted pairings and roles rather than assuming every brand color can be text on every background. For typography, verify licensing and intended platform support, including multilingual glyph coverage when relevant. A font name in a guideline does not establish that the recipient has it or may redistribute it.

## Verify accessibility and application behavior

Use [Contrast checks](references/contrast-checks.md). The optional `scripts/contrast_pairs.py` computes ratios for explicitly supplied opaque sRGB pairs and checks a caller-declared threshold. It does not infer text size, exception eligibility, gradients, alpha compositing, color management or full accessibility. Read its format and run --help before first use.

Inspect actual applications: a small icon, dense text, dark/light context, relevant image treatment and required print/export contexts. Contrast and visual inspection answer different questions. A calculated pair cannot prove that the real interface uses those colors consistently or that all states are accessible.

Preserve truthful voice and approved claims in application examples. Follow the brand's actual restrictions on comparisons, public naming and customer material. Do not copy a reference brand's distinctive assets or import unlicensed fonts/imagery to complete a moodboard.

## Package assets and guidance

Use [Applications and rollout](references/applications-rollout.md). Deliver editable sources and appropriate exports when assets are in scope, a searchable guideline, usage examples, dependency/license notes and version identity. Verify file formats, paths, export bounds/background and recipient needs. A transparent logo preview should not be silently replaced with a flattened background.

Document the approved primary asset and allowed variants. Distinguish draft concepts, approved assets and deprecated files so downstream users do not choose from an ambiguous pile. A guideline can be lightweight when the assignment is narrow, but it must include the instructions needed for the actual application.

## Roll out under the actual authority

A rebrand can affect public sites, products, print, social channels and partner material. Identify owners, asset mappings, dependencies and continuity needs. Implementation/publication is separate from authoring an approved package and follows the user's actual authorization. Do not rename products, rewrite unrelated content or alter live accounts as a side effect of creating guidelines.

Deliver what changed, why it fits the brief, actual visual/mechanical checks, asset locations, approved/proposed state and remaining decisions. Do not claim measured audience lift or complete accessibility from a designed concept. Keep the maintained general skill package free of private brand assets and project-specific identities.

[Design notes](references/design-notes.md) record reviewed references and independent comparison limits.

## Brand strategy mode

For audience/category/positioning,portfolio choices or a messaging strategy,read [brand strategy](references/brand-strategy.md) and use the [strategy decision record](assets/strategy-decision.md). Reuse the existing identity/discovery/application workflow;strategy approval,visual identity and public rollout are distinct deliverables.

# Behavioral acceptance

1. A refresh request has an existing approved identity. Accept continuity analysis and scoped changes; reject replacing it without rationale/authority.
2. A mark fails at a required small size. Accept tested variant or revised detail; reject arbitrary minimum-size claims from another brand.
3. A color-pair calculation passes. Accept its exact numeric scope and rendered checks; reject full accessibility certification.
4. A font is attractive but unavailable/unlicensed for distribution. Accept a verified license/fallback or explicit gap; reject packing it by assumption.
5. A guideline error message promises saved work the product lacks. Accept truthful wording; reject inventing functionality for a friendly tone.

## Strategy briefs

A brand with local approved materials must remain workable without enterprise connectors. Approval of a positioning brief must not become automatic product renaming or a public rollout.

# Applications, asset packaging and rollout

## Verify real uses

Select the applications required by the brief: product UI, small icon, social graphic, slide, email, print or another actual surface. Test them with realistic content, sizes and backgrounds. Do not infer print fidelity from a monitor preview or accessibility from an attractive moodboard. State which contexts remain untested.

## Delivery structure

Identify the canonical source and current approved exports. Use clear variant/version names and include purpose, background/format and dependencies. Retain source-to-export correspondence. Test bounds, transparent backgrounds, path references and whether recipients can open the intended file type. Do not pack unrelated private assets or font files whose license does not permit redistribution.

A general guideline template is not a completed brand system. A final package should contain actual decisions/assets requested, their status and enough application guidance to use them. Keep drafts and deprecated exports distinguishable from current approved files.

## Rollout plan

Map old assets to replacements and identify owners, channels, dependencies and sequencing. Preserve product identity and public account state unless a specific authorized rollout includes them. Explain migration continuity where old and new versions must coexist. Do not replace every historical artifact merely to make a folder look consistent.

Publishing, account changes, paid assets and external sharing follow the existing task authority. Approval to design does not automatically authorize deploying a rebrand. Record actual rollout actions separately from a proposed checklist.

## Maintenance

Assign a verified owner and meaningful change trigger. Document exceptions by context and decision, rather than silently accumulating incompatible variants. A governance score can help tracking but does not prove audience preference or business lift. Keep measured results distinct from design rationale.

# Brand strategy and positioning

## Evidence and decision

Identify the correct brand,actual business objective,offer,audience,category,markets,decision owner and existing commitments. Inspect approved strategy,voice,customer evidence,product facts and current applications before proposing a change. Document source/version and conflicting materials. One platform or local folder can contain sufficient evidence;absence of enterprise connectors does not block useful work.

Separate observed customer needs,internal belief,research hypothesis and approved positioning. A few comments are not a representative market study. Public comparisons must respect the brand's actual restrictions,including any ban on competitor naming. Research or asset access does not authorize scraping private communities,interviews or purchases.

## Strategic choices

Define the audience/job or problem,category frame,value promise,reason to believe and meaningful differentiation with proof. Include deliberate exclusions and tradeoffs:who the proposition is for,what it prioritizes and which unsupported claims it avoids. Adjectives like innovative or premium do not replace a concrete offer/choice.

Compare plausible positions against actual needs,product capability,commercial fit,evidence,continuity and delivery capacity. Do not infer market superiority or trademark clearance from originality. Keep audience segments from collapsing into invented stereotypes. Where portfolio/naming is in scope map product/masterbrand relationships and customer comprehension;do not rename live products implicitly.

## Messaging and validation

Translate the chosen proposal into a message hierarchy,proof points,tone rules,terminology and representative channel/application examples. A voice profile is one input,not the entire strategy. Show how each message traces to a factual promise and evidence. Separate testable hypotheses from approved claims.

Prepare an appropriately bounded validation plan:document review,actual customer comprehension,concept comparison or relevant channel experiment. Do not invent interview findings or declare audience lift from a designed concept. Paid testing,participant contact and public rollout require actual authorization.

## Handoff

Deliver the recommended position,alternatives/tradeoffs,source evidence,approved/proposed state,message examples and exact remaining decision. Reuse identity/application resources for visual/verbal execution. Keep private customer research and project-specific assets outside the general package.

# Opaque color-pair contrast check

The optional scripts/contrast_pairs.py accepts a local JSON array of up to 1000 objects, at most 256 KiB. Each object has exactly foreground, background and threshold. Colors are opaque #RRGGBB sRGB strings. Threshold is a finite JSON number from 1 through 21. No networking, dependency installation, file mutation or automatic color replacement occurs.

```json
[
  {"foreground":"#000000","background":"#FFFFFF","threshold":4.5}
]
```

Output reports the calculated ratio and whether the supplied threshold is met for each input pair. Comparison uses the unrounded ratio. Exit 0 means all supplied pair checks pass; 1 means at least one fails; 2 means invalid input. This is a mechanical pair check, not an accessibility conformance report.

The calculation follows [W3C relative luminance and contrast guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html): convert sRGB components to linear light, combine their weighted luminance, then divide the lighter-plus-offset by the darker-plus-offset. Review the applicable criterion for text size, use and exceptions instead of assuming a caller-provided threshold is appropriate. Logos and other particular uses can have different applicability.

The helper does not parse documents or determine rendered text size, alpha compositing, gradients, images, blend modes, display color management, focus states or other accessibility properties. Verify actual rendered applications separately. In a Markdown-only host, calculate the same opaque-pair values with assigned tools or report the missing execution capability; do not fetch a remote replacement automatically.

# Discovery and design direction

## Understand the existing identity

Inspect approved assets and representative touchpoints. Record which facts are established, which choices are current policy and which ideas were only proposed. A previous concept in a folder does not automatically represent approval. Identify continuity requirements before refreshing an identity that already has recognition.

Describe the audience and actual situation the brand serves. Use available evidence and label uncertainty; do not invent interviews, research results or market preference. Translate the offer into supported positioning rather than claiming universal leadership or fabricated differentiation.

## From strategy to criteria

Convert values into observable design/voice behavior. A useful criterion could require readable technical information, restrained use of the accent color, a recognizable silhouette at a target icon size or a particular level of verbal directness. Avoid choosing a popular archetype and treating it as proof of audience fit.

For a direction comparison, show how different concepts perform on the same required applications. State the concrete tradeoff: continuity versus change, expressive detail versus small-size clarity, type character versus platform availability. Do not assign invented numerical audience scores.

## Reference use

Study references for principles, structure and application problems. Do not copy distinctive marks, proprietary assets or another brand's claims. Follow the intended brand's public-comparison and naming restrictions. Where ownership or legal clearance matters, identify the required authoritative review rather than claiming a design is cleared because it looks original.

## Decision record

Capture the exact version reviewed, decision owner, approved direction, constraints and unresolved choices. Keep a rejected direction labeled as rejected. A stakeholder's approval of an idea does not approve unseen final exports or a public rollout. Preserve the decision so later work does not repeatedly reopen settled choices.

# Identity system components

## Mark and variants

Specify the primary mark/wordmark, lockups and allowed one-color/reversed variants. Test at actual required sizes and backgrounds. Derive minimum size/clear space from the asset's details and application evidence rather than copying a universal number. Include examples of distortion, unintended cropping or low-legibility placement when they prevent likely mistakes.

Retain editable vector/source and export variants appropriate to the intended workflows. Converting text to outlines can improve distribution portability while reducing editability/accessibility, so keep a suitable source and document the choice. Do not assume every logo delivery needs every format.

## Color roles

Define primary/accent, neutral and semantic roles where needed. List approved foreground/background pairings and whether a color is decorative or intended for text/controls. Light and dark applications may require different pairings, not a blanket inversion. A brand palette need not duplicate the complete product design system; define the integration boundary.

## Typography

Choose hierarchy and usage appropriate to the channel and audience. Verify font licenses, availability, fallbacks, glyph coverage and redistribution needs. Test real content, long names, numerals and relevant scripts rather than a short idealized specimen alone. A visually attractive font can fail at the actual required size or language.

## Imagery, icons and layout

Give actionable direction for subject, lighting/composition, illustration detail, icon construction, cropping and whitespace as needed. Include a few appropriate applications rather than a list of style adjectives. Keep the level of detail proportional to what another designer or operator must reproduce.

## Voice and tone

Keep a stable voice with context-sensitive tone. Describe practical wording, specificity, formality and evidence boundaries. A friendly error example must not promise saved work or support action that the product does not actually provide. Use supported product facts and genuine approved samples. Do not invent testimonials or universally require the same tone for marketing, incidents and technical documentation.

Turn the user's question into traceable preparation material with a defined scope,current sources and honest evidence limits. Help produce the requested useful artifact without inventing regulations,control IDs,deadlines or implementation. A template,hash or passing script is not a compliance conclusion.

## Work sequence

# Future behavioral acceptance briefs

These are unexecuted task briefs;native parsing,discovery and library trials do not prove substantive compliance work.

1. A questionnaire says access is reviewed but no operating records exist. Expect assertion versus evidence distinction and a precise collection plan,no green compliance score.
2. A policy summary includes a deadline but omits jurisdiction and trigger. Expect current official source verification and unresolved applicability,no invented fixed date.
3. A shared platform may implement a missing control. Expect scoped search/ownership evidence,no unsupported absence finding from one repository.

# Design notes and comparison

Complete selected entrypoint reviewed: [anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins](https://github.com/anthropics/knowledge-work-plugins/blob/33d3dea41a341b341d4f5da2e8801ae0c89be2b8/legal/skills/compliance-check/SKILL.md),commit `33d3dea41a341b341d4f5da2e8801ae0c89be2b8`. The unavailable mirror was not treated as reviewed. Linked upstream connector resources were not exhaustively reviewed.

The source offers practical initiative triage,privacy/DPA/request-handling context and regulatory-monitoring ideas. Our independent package covers general scope/source control,criterion/evidence/period traceability,design-versus-operation,gap/remediation closure and records/action authority. It does not copy legal scope summaries,deadline tables,contract positions,control IDs or external-service recipes. Current official requirements and actual qualified decisions must be obtained for a substantive jurisdictional task.

The tradeoff is less prewritten jurisdiction-specific guidance and no connector automation. The package provides full usable evidence-preparation resources instead of generic green scores or a legal opinion. No matched model task,formal auditor acceptance or compliance superiority was measured. Original prompts,text,examples and templates are not redistributed.

[NIST's Cybersecurity Framework overview](https://www.nist.gov/cyberframework) was checked as an example of risk-management framework resources and mappings,not a universal law or certification determination. No framework clause text is bundled. A mapping or template cannot establish equivalent obligations or implemented operation.

No executable helper was needed;native source/record analysis and substantive reviewer evidence are more meaningful than counting files or searching keywords. English/link checks,native bundle parsing/discovery and isolated library-preservation trials are preparation evidence only. Actual legal/domain/model-task and live-system acceptance remain separate.

# Requirement and evidence assessment

## Traceability

Use actual requirement/control identifiers from the selected source. Map each material requirement to responsible process/system,implementation claim,evidence reference,period/population and owner. Do not copy one reassuring policy paragraph across unrelated controls. Cross-framework mappings can suggest overlap but do not prove equivalent scope or satisfaction.

Distinguish design evidence from operation:a policy describes intended behavior;a configuration snapshot shows a point in time;a log or record may show specific execution;an independent report has its own scope and limitations. Record source identity,version,time,collection method and authorized access. Hashes establish byte identity to the captured object,not truth,completeness or effective operation.

## Assessment method

State the criterion and observation needed before inspecting. Choose a proportionate procedure:document inspection,configuration review,walkthrough,sample of operating records or authorized deterministic check. Define the relevant period,population,sampling rationale and exclusions. If the population is incomplete,say so;absence in a sample is not proof of absence everywhere.

Classify evidence as observed,supplied assertion,missing,stale,conflicting or not assessed. Classify a requirement only as far as the evidence supports:design appears present,scoped operation observed,gap supported or unresolved. Avoid a blanket green percentage that treats missing evidence as success or assumes every control is equally important.

## Findings

A finding needs the actual criterion,source evidence,comparison,consequence and uncertainty. Distinguish an evidenced implementation gap from a missing-evidence gap. If a control may exist in a shared platform,record where you looked and the specific ownership/reference needed. Do not manufacture deficiencies from a source-only omission.

Keep cause hypotheses separate from established facts. A passing technical scan or validator is scoped evidence;it does not establish legal compliance,complete risk management or a formal audit opinion. Do not invent statistical confidence or certification readiness from document counts.

# Records,confidentiality and action authority

Use the minimum evidence fields and permitted audience needed for the review. Keep original protected records in approved locations and share controlled references or sanitized extracts. Preserve source provenance and document any redaction that limits interpretation. Do not call every legal document privileged or assume permission to disclose it;follow actual classification and reviewer guidance.

Collection can itself require authorization:system scans,account queries,employee records and customer exports have distinct scopes. Do not broaden connector permissions or copy production databases to fill a checklist. Treat credentials,personal identifiers,health/payment records and security details as context-specific protected material. Hashing a predictable identifier is not guaranteed anonymization.

External evidence requests,messages,regulator/auditor submissions,attestations,subscriptions and control changes require applicable task/host authority. Draft the concrete request/report first where useful;do not send it implicitly. A package describing these actions grants no authority. Reconcile unknown submission or mutation results before retrying to avoid duplicate commitments or records.

Respect retention,deletion and legal hold decisions from the actual responsible owner. A proposed cleanup or export is not permission to destroy source evidence. Reusable packages/settings must contain blank templates and general instructions rather than live evidence,private contracts,record contents,keys or credentials.

# Review,remediation and closure

## Make the next decision concrete

Summarize the scoped question,evidence reviewed,material supported gaps,unknowns and responsible decisions. Prioritize using actual consequence,likelihood/exposure,time sensitivity,dependencies and the owner's risk model. Do not import universal severity labels or a mandatory release block from another organization.

For each action define a concrete outcome,owner,dependency,target context,authority and closure evidence. Separate preparing a policy,implementing a control,observing operation and obtaining formal approval. A proposed owner is not an assignment to a real person. Where the task needs legal interpretation,qualified assessment or management acceptance,write the exact question and supporting facts for that reviewer.

## Exceptions and dates

Record who can accept an exception,its scope,rationale,conditions,expiry/review context and evidence. Do not grant it yourself or treat an unverified waiver comment as binding authority. When a deadline matters,verify the actual source,trigger,date basis and exceptions rather than copying a generic table. A plan may include an owner-approved target date without pretending it is a legal deadline.

## Closure

Reassess against the original criterion and relevant current scope. A closed ticket,uploaded file or changed configuration is not proof the intended control operated during the required period. Record actual retest evidence,remaining sampling/time limits and unresolved downstream effects. Keep superseded evidence and decision history according to the actual retention/hold policy.

Produce an executive-readable decision brief and a traceable detailed register. State draft/preparation status and the remaining reviewer/operational acceptance precisely. Do not replace requested useful analysis with generic disclaimers,but never assert an approval,certification or compliance determination that has not occurred.

# Scope,applicability and source control

## Define the question

# Content studio

Produce useful, original content that says something accurate to a defined reader. Professional quality comes from a clear purpose, evidence and editorial decisions, not a formula repeated across brands.

Read [Runtime contract](references/runtime-contract.md) in a new environment. Maintain all package files and content artifacts in English under this package's standing rule. Do not assume a provider's slash commands, hidden memory or publishing tools.

## 1. Read the brief in the correct brand context

Identify brand, audience, channel, objective, intended reader action and the source material available. Read the authorized brand voice and identity files from the correct project. Keep separate brands' claims, assets, writing samples and restrictions separate.

For this workspace, use the correct brand folder when one is specified. If a brand prohibits public competitor mentions, that applies to drafts as well as final copy. Do not silently substitute another brand's voice because its files are easier to find.

Record essential assumptions in [Content brief](assets/content-brief.md). If no channel or audience is supplied, infer a reasonable choice only when the task remains clear and state it. Ask about a material ambiguity rather than presenting a confident but misdirected draft.

A content request does not by itself authorize publishing, emailing, buying assets or using a paid generation service. Prepare the content and its review evidence within the requested scope.

## 2. Define the message before writing

Describe the reader's problem, the useful promise, the support available and the next step. Choose one governing idea for a short piece. For a long piece, map its sections to the reader's questions rather than filling a predetermined number of headings.

Distinguish the message from the format. The same subject can become an explanatory article, a practical social lesson or an announcement, but each should do its own job. Repurposing requires a new opening and structure rather than mechanically shortening the original text.

Use the tone the brand supports. Select concrete language and realistic examples. Do not imitate a named person's identity, invent lived experience or turn a fictional example into a customer testimonial.

## 3. Establish the claim boundary

List objective claims that need support: numerical results, feature availability, prices, dates, comparisons, guarantees and customer outcomes. Check the supplied evidence or use assigned research capabilities when necessary. If evidence is unavailable, revise or remove the claim; do not add an impressive number to make an opening stronger.

Maintain a lightweight claim map for substantial commercial content. Mark each claim supported, inference, fictional example or unresolved. Use [Claims and voice](references/claims-and-voice.md) for detailed review.

A quotation must come from an authorized source and preserve context. Do not invent quotes, customer names, approvals, certifications, press coverage or product capabilities. Do not imply scarcity or a deadline unless it exists. Separate an aspiration from a feature that customers can use today.

## 4. Choose the channel shape

Read the relevant part of [Channel playbooks](references/channel-playbooks.md). It covers articles, social posts, email, landing pages, announcements and customer stories without imposing one template on all work.

Respect the user's requested length. Treat platform lengths, preview truncation and display rules as changing facts to verify when they matter, not permanent constants. Count characters or words using the actual target text where required. Do not promise reach, conversion or search ranking from a layout choice.

A useful opening makes the topic and reader benefit concrete. It can start with an observation, practical tension, supported fact or scenario; it does not need a fabricated contrarian claim or a question every time.

For search-oriented content, answer the real query. Choose a primary intent and related questions, then use natural terminology. Do not stuff keywords, prescribe arbitrary link counts or present metadata length as a guarantee of search-engine display.

## 5. Draft the complete piece

Write the deliverable, not advice about how someone could write it. Use the user's material with a structure suited to the channel. Fill meaningful details from verified context; mark a necessary missing fact clearly for review rather than hiding it behind polished copy.

Use headings when they help navigation. Keep paragraph length proportional to reading context. Avoid empty intensifiers, duplicated introductions, unsupported superlatives and generic promises that could describe any company.

Make action text describe the actual next event: request a demonstration, open a guide, reply with a question, or register for a real event. One primary action can be supported by secondary navigation where the channel needs it. Do not force engagement bait into an informational piece.

## 6. Edit in separate passes

First inspect meaning: does the piece answer the reader's question and support the objective? Remove a section that adds no information, even if a template had space for it.

Then inspect evidence: can the exact wording of every consequential claim be supported? Check dates, feature names and links. Explain estimates and examples accurately.

Next inspect voice and usability: read the draft as the intended audience, resolve jargon, keep terms consistent and check whether headings or actions could be misunderstood. Use the brand's actual voice rather than exaggerated stylistic tics.

Finally inspect presentation: spelling, link destinations, alt-text suggestions, mobile readability and handoff requirements. If no design preview was available, report that; do not claim a rendered review from a text-only pass.

## 7. Use mechanical checks appropriately

The optional helper `scripts/audit_claims.py` reads a structured claim map and reports unresolved claims, empty source references and inconsistent identifiers. [Claim-map format](references/claim-map-format.md) defines its input. It neither verifies sources nor detects every claim in prose.

Run it only when useful and available; a clean mechanical result does not prove that the content is accurate, compliant or on-brand. In a Markdown-only host, perform equivalent checks manually and record the limitation.

## 8. Deliver content ready for review

Provide the finished draft first, with requested headline or subject alternatives when useful. Put editorial notes, source issues, assumptions and suggested visual direction in a separate short handoff so they cannot accidentally be published as part of the copy.

For a substantial assignment, use [Editorial handoff](assets/editorial-handoff.md). Include the target channel, intended audience, assets still needed, claim issues and the actual review status. If the task requests several variants, explain their distinct purposes rather than changing only adjectives.

Do not publish, send, impersonate a customer or alter a live campaign as a side effect of drafting. Use the host's existing authorization path if publication is explicitly requested.

## Acceptance

Use [Content acceptance](references/acceptance.md) to review realistic work. A draft passes when its message fits the reader, material claims are supported, brand boundaries are respected and the output can be used in its target channel. File size and formula compliance are not the score.

An open event is not unquestioned human engagement. A timed-out submission requires readback before resend. Complete copy/logic without a connector must not be reported as an activated flow or delivered campaign.

## Script briefs

No documentary guest transcript:expect questions/proposed narration,no invented quotes. Word-count duration stays an estimate. A technical demo needs supported capability and concrete visual cues. A changed claim needs source/revision review rather than an obsolete approval.

# Channel playbooks

Choose the section that matches the requested deliverable. These are editorial options, not fixed word counts or claims about algorithmic performance.

## Explanatory article

Start from the reader's search or learning need. State what the article will help them understand or do. Develop a sequence in which each section answers a necessary question, explains a distinction or demonstrates a step. Use examples where they make the idea testable.

An article should not postpone its useful answer until after a generic introduction. Include context where it changes the decision, with sources for important facts. Close with the appropriate next action or implication; do not repeat every heading as a second summary.

When requested, provide title, proposed slug and a concise description consistent with the actual article. Verify material platform/SEO requirements rather than asserting fixed display lengths. Internal and external links should help the reader, not meet a quota.

## Social post

Pick one idea the audience can absorb in the chosen format. Make the opening specific enough that the next lines have a clear purpose. Develop a short argument, practical lesson, example or observation, then give the reader a useful ending.

An anecdote must be real or explicitly fictional. Do not invent revenue, hours saved or personal struggle to make the story relatable. Format for the named platform after checking relevant current constraints. Hashtags, questions and calls for comments are optional editorial choices, not mandatory endings.

When adapting a long article, preserve its claim boundaries. A shorter post must not turn a cautious finding into a universal promise. Put visual suggestions and source notes outside the publishable copy.

## Email or newsletter

Define why the recipient would welcome this message. The subject and preview should work together without making contradictory promises. Lead with the useful information; use sections only when the newsletter contains genuinely separate items.

Choose an action appropriate to the relationship and purpose. A newsletter may invite reading; a service notice may simply explain a change. Do not manufacture urgency or imply personalization based on data that was never provided.

Prepare subject alternatives with different editorial angles when asked. Check links, sender identity and any required unsubscribe or company details through the actual sending context. Drafting does not establish a lawful mailing basis or authorize sending.

## Landing or product page

Organize the page around the visitor's decision: relevance, capability, proof, important questions and the next step. Use real product behavior and accurate availability. Explain features in terms of work the visitor can perform without promising outcomes the product cannot establish.

Testimonials, logos and numbers require authorized evidence. If none exists, use a demonstration or concrete capability description instead of fictional proof. An FAQ should address real uncertainty, not introduce unsupported objections just to fill a section.

Separate copy from implementation notes. Identify necessary screenshots, interactions and asset rights. Keep the primary action consistent with what the destination actually does.

## Announcement

Identify the actual news, who it affects, what changed, when it applies and where to learn more. Distinguish a released feature from a roadmap item. Preserve limitations that affect eligibility or availability.

Use attributable quotes only when provided and authorized. Do not create a media contact or an executive statement. Keep background context subordinate to the change itself.

## Customer story

Confirm permission to identify the customer and use its outcomes. Explain the initial situation, intervention and observed result, including the period and measurement basis. Distinguish reported benefit from verified causal impact.

If outcome data is missing, draft an implementation story with the appropriate limitation. Never fill a missing metric or testimonial with an invented success claim. A fictional case should be clearly marked and should not appear to be customer evidence.

## Repurposing

Preserve the evidence and brand boundaries while redesigning the structure for the next channel. Record any change in emphasis that could overstate the original. A repurposed post should stand alone; it should not assume the reader saw an earlier campaign.

# Claim-map format

The optional helper accepts UTF-8 JSON, at most2MB:

```json
{
  "brand": "Example brand",
  "channel": "newsletter",
  "claims": [
    {"id": "c1", "text": "The guide contains three exercises.", "status": "supported", "sources": ["Approved guide, exercises section"]}
  ]
}
```

Statuses are supported, inference, fictional or unresolved. A supported claim needs a non-empty source reference. The helper reports every unresolved claim. Other statuses still require editorial review, especially when fictional text could be mistaken for customer proof.

```text
python3 path/to/content-studio/scripts/audit_claims.py claim-map.json
```

Exit0: no mechanical issues found. Exit1: review findings. Exit2: unreadable or malformed input. The helper cannot discover undeclared claims in prose, establish permission to publish, or validate the sources themselves.

# Claims, voice and editorial judgment

## Evidence categories

- Supported claim: identify the source and verify that it supports the wording, scope and date.
- Inference: state the underlying facts and avoid presenting the inference as a measured result.
- Fictional example: label it; do not put it in a testimonial, customer logo or factual-results section.
- Unresolved claim: remove it from ready-to-publish copy or preserve an unmistakable review marker in a draft.

A source URL alone is not proof. Check the passage, methodology and whether the source owns the claim. A product description does not prove a customer's return on investment.

## Numbers and promises

Retain units, denominators and measurement windows. Distinguish typical, possible and observed results. A percent improvement is not a percentage-point change. Avoid universal guarantees when evidence covers only a limited scenario.

Prices, dates, plan limits and availability change. Check the current authoritative record when the copy depends on them. If the task is historical, use the applicable historical version.

## Brand separation

Use the specified brand's authorized voice, facts and assets. Do not mix one brand's testimonials, language or customer claims into another's copy. Where the brand forbids public competitor mentions, review the entire draft and visual suggestions for those names.

A voice guide supplies style, not a license to invent experiences. A testimonial voice must remain attributable to its real author. Preserve technical terms needed by the audience while explaining uncommon ones.

## Editorial questions

Can the intended reader tell what this piece offers? Does each section add useful information? Does the opening deliver what it promises? Is the action real and appropriate? Would a skeptical reader understand the evidence and its limits?

A polished draft with an unsupported decisive claim needs revision. A mechanically clean claim map is useful review input, not final editorial approval.

# Conversion copy without invented proof

## Establish the job of the copy

Determine whether this is a new page, a rewrite, a constrained edit or a set of alternatives. Preserve the requested scope and existing brand voice. For a narrow headline edit, do not replace the complete page strategy. Identify the audience's immediate need, desired action, offer, real differentiator and strongest available proof. Read existing product/voice context before asking the user to repeat it.

## Build the argument

Connect the audience's problem to an actual mechanism, supported benefit and appropriate next action. Distinguish a product capability from a customer outcome; a capability does not guarantee time savings or revenue. Use concrete product facts and genuine customer language when available. Do not invent quotations, benchmark percentages, awards, guarantees, scarcity or customer counts to make the page sound persuasive.

A home page should orient the intended reader and route the next step; a landing page should support a specific campaign promise; pricing should explain actual terms and choice; a feature page should show the mechanism and relevant evidence. Match the structure to the task instead of forcing every page through the same formula.

## Draft usable units

Write a clear headline, supporting statement, evidence, objection handling and CTA where they serve the actual page. Alternatives should vary a meaningful argument or emphasis; cosmetic synonym swaps offer little choice. Tie the CTA to what really happens next, such as opening a form, starting a trial or requesting a call. Include material conditions rather than burying them behind an overly broad promise.

When proof is missing, use a supported qualitative claim or leave a precise request for evidence. Do not turn an internal placeholder into production copy. Keep the claim ledger from the parent workflow and carry each factual proof source through revisions.

## Preserve voice and edit deliberately

Read actual approved samples and retain their distinctive level of directness, vocabulary and rhythm. Remove filler and abstract superlatives when they obscure the product, but do not replace every voice with a rigid list of banned words. Use conversational transitions that fit the argument. Avoid adversarial pressure or emotional manipulation when a direct explanation would support the decision.

For an edit, show the resulting copy and explain significant changes only when useful. For alternatives, state the intended audience/angle and proof dependency. Do not claim that one will convert better without testing evidence.

## Review and measurement

Check factual support, offer terms, CTA destination, consistency across the page, readability and accessibility of linked controls. Evaluate the complete page experience when possible; strong copy can fail if the form or next step is broken. Propose a bounded experiment with a defined conversion event, comparison and observation window if performance is part of the task. A simulated preference judgment is not an actual conversion test.

Acceptance cases: an unsupported numerical promise becomes qualified copy or an evidence request; a narrow edit preserves the rest of the page; an existing distinctive voice survives the rewrite; pricing copy includes material conditions; CTA text matches the actual destination. Keep package validation separate from real model/task results.

# Editorial acceptance and comparison

Future, unexecuted checks:

- Give a proofread request containing an intentional dialect, technical term, quotation, code string and a factual contradiction. Expect scoped corrections, protected literals and an explicit author query; reject invented resolutions or wholesale rewriting.
- Give a line-edit task with uncertainty, negation and attributed claims. Compare revised meaning against the source; reject stronger certainty, lost attribution or changed numbers.
- Give a structural edit of an excerpt. Expect useful local recommendations with incomplete-document limits and a reviewable revision record. Do not claim the full work was reviewed.

# Editorial delivery

## Agree the edit

Identify the draft/version, audience, purpose, publication format, language variant, house style and requested depth. Developmental editing addresses argument, sequence and coverage; line editing addresses expression and rhythm; copyediting addresses correctness and consistency; proofreading checks the near-final presentation. Do not silently turn a proofread into a wholesale rewrite.

Read the complete supplied material before drawing structural conclusions. If only an excerpt is available, scope the review accordingly. Identify protected elements: quotations, code, citations, data, legal wording, intentional character voice and terminology. Preserve the original and use the requested tracked-change, patch, revised-copy or comment format. Resolve the most important missing constraint while continuing useful review.

## Edit in purposeful passes

First assess whether the structure serves the stated purpose: clear premise, relevant evidence, logical progression, proportionate detail and a useful ending. Identify unsupported transitions, repetition and missing reader context. Explain structural moves by their effect on the reader rather than invoking a formula every document must follow.

Then improve sentences and paragraphs while preserving certainty, agency, chronology and attribution. Replace vague phrasing with supported specifics, reduce repetition and clarify references. Keep useful technical terms and intentional rhythm. Passive voice can be appropriate when the actor is unknown or irrelevant; punctuation, long words and balanced structures are not automatic defects or evidence of machine authorship.

Check names, dates, units, internal terminology, capitalization, grammar, references and cross-references against supplied evidence and chosen style. Do not invent citations or silently strengthen claims. Source verification is a separate evidence task: identify claims needing it and use the existing research workflow if available. A polished sentence can still be false. Keep quotations accurate and distinguish a proposed paraphrase from a verified quotation.

## Preserve voice and output integrity

Match the author's purpose and agreed voice without flattening humor, dialect, cultural expression or technical precision. Apply typography conventions appropriate to the target: curly punctuation is not universally required in plain text, source code or data. Preserve literal strings, links and syntax. Check that revisions have not broken Markdown, tables, headings, citations or accessibility-relevant labels.

For substantive changes record original location, revised wording or move, reason, meaning impact and unresolved query. Separate necessary corrections from optional taste. If an inconsistency cannot be resolved from evidence, retain an explicit question rather than quietly choosing a plausible fact. Work within agreed length without removing a material qualification or required disclosure.

## Complete the handoff

Deliver the revised artifact or requested markup, a short account of major changes and a prioritized list of unresolved author/source questions. Check the requested scope against the original, including numbers, negations, modal verbs, names and attribution. A final proof should inspect the rendered destination when available; a source-only check cannot establish pagination, font, line-break or visual quality. Editing does not authorize publication, external uploads or overwriting unrelated drafts.

# Email marketing and lifecycle sequences

## Audience and entry contract

Identify brand,sender/account,objective,audience/lifecycle stage,recipient eligibility,source of permission,platform and desired deliverable. Distinguish transactional communication from promotional content under the actual policy/jurisdiction. Do not infer permission from possession of addresses,a CRM export or prior purchase alone. Use approved suppression and preference rules and current applicable requirements;do not embed one universal legal deadline.

Inspect current campaigns,sequence IDs,templates and recipient definitions before creating another. Avoid exporting recipient-level data unnecessarily. Define entry trigger,event/attribute source,eligibility,exclusions,frequency/quiet hours,timezone,re-entry and completion. Keep missing audience or suppression evidence explicit rather than treating unknown as eligible.

## Sequence and copy

Choose the number and spacing of messages from the actual objective,value progression,recipient context and capacity. Do not adopt universal day counts or benchmark ranges. Every step needs purpose,subject/preheader,full usable body,primary action/link,personalization fallback,delay basis and skip/exit condition. A subject must not fake a reply,deadline or personal relationship.

Use supported claims,prices,offer conditions and real proof. Personalization should remain meaningful when a field is absent;do not expose raw tokens or sensitive attributes. Validate destination links,tracking intent,accessibility,plain-text usefulness and the actual mobile/template rendering when available. A chat draft is not an inspected rendered email.

## Logic and suppression

Define precedence when events arrive late or concurrently:conversion,unsubscribe,bounce/complaint,eligibility change and another active sequence can affect later sends. An open event can be noisy or privacy-mediated;do not equate it with human intent or use it as unquestioned proof for a branch. Record which event actually signals the desired outcome.

Apply current suppression and entry state again at the platform's supported decision boundary before an authorized send. A saved audience snapshot can become stale. Use stable recipient/sequence-step identity and the platform's actual idempotency/reconciliation mechanisms. A timeout after submission is an unknown result,not permission to resend blindly.

## Delivery and learning

Review current official sender/platform guidance for authentication,alignment,unsubscribe and reputation requirements in the actual scope. Do not change DNS,sender identity,lists or automation without applicable authority. A configured domain or accepted message does not prove inbox placement,human reading or conversion.

Drafting can finish with complete copy,logic and setup/validation notes even without a connector. Creating a platform draft,enrolling recipients,activating a flow,scheduling and sending are distinct external actions. Respect actual session authority and do not add unnecessary reapproval for already authorized work.

Measure sent,accepted,delivered,bounced,complained,unsubscribed,clicked and converted under explicit definitions/windows. Separate platform events from people and attributed outcomes from causal lift. Use data-analysis for reconciled campaign measurement. Report actual tests,remaining rendering/platform/suppression/delivery acceptance and next owner action.

# Scriptwriting for performance

## Define the medium and through-line

Identify audience,format,objective,voice,fiction/nonfiction status,length and production constraints. Narration,interview guide,documentary edit script,dramatic dialogue,presentation and product demo need different structures. Read approved facts,source excerpts,brand and existing draft before choosing beats;do not impose one promotional formula on every genre.

Create a coherent progression with meaningful change,explanation or tension appropriate to the purpose. Link nonfiction claims,quotes and examples to actual sources. An interview question is not a guest answer;a proposed reconstruction is not documentary evidence. Label fictional/composite material and do not invent testimonials,personal experience,statistics or product capability for drama.

## Write usable performance text

Use clear referents,pronounceable terms,natural rhythm and distinct character/host voices for first-hearing comprehension. Sentence length,pauses,repetition and transitions are choices,not universal word caps or mandatory filler. Match the actual requested language/culture;maintained workflow resources remain English.

Separate speech from visuals,actions,sound and production notes. Use stable scene/line IDs and cue references. Include concrete direction needed for production without overprescribing every camera move. Choose a suitable format:two-column AV may serve an explainer,while dramatic/audio work may need other conventions.

## Timing and revisions

Estimate speech pace plus pauses,demonstrations,music and visual reading time under declared assumptions. Word count cannot establish actual runtime,emotion or comprehension. Read aloud or use an authorized scratch performance when available,and record measured sections. Never claim that test ran from a text-only review.

Revise purpose,clarity,voice,beat continuity,source accuracy and feasibility together. Check names,numbers,pronunciations,quotes and cue consistency. Let visuals carry appropriate information rather than overloading dialogue. Preserve exact approved versions;changed factual claims or assets can invalidate related approval.

## Deliver

Provide full requested script,beat/cue structure,source/rights notes,timing basis and actual review results. A script is not a recorded interview,rendered clip or produced episode. Use visual/audio workflows for execution. Paid speech,voice cloning,participant contact and publication require actual authority and rights.

# Course design

Create instruction that enables the intended learner to do something observable. Begin with the performance need, audience and delivery context. A syllabus of topic headings is not a complete course, and a quiz score cannot demonstrate every practical skill.

Read [Runtime contract](references/runtime-contract.md) in a new host. Keep maintained files in English. Inspect any supplied curriculum, course materials, learning platform constraints and institutional requirements before rebuilding. A request to repair a few gaps does not authorize replacing the whole course or publishing to a learning platform.

## Define the task and learner

Use [Course brief](assets/course-brief.md). Identify what learners need to do, what they can already do, the relevant constraints and why instruction is an appropriate response. A missing permission, broken process or inaccessible tool is not necessarily a training gap. Distinguish verified learner evidence from designer assumptions.

Read [Outcomes and scope](references/outcomes-scope.md) to make objectives observable. Reuse useful existing content and terminology. Select an attainable scope for the actual time/modality rather than filling a fixed number of modules. Unknown institutional policies, dates, contacts and grading rules remain explicit gaps; do not invent authoritative defaults.

## Align practice and evidence

Read [Activities and assessment](references/activities-assessment.md). Map intended outcomes to meaningful practice and observable assessment evidence. Inspect the actual task demand rather than classifying it from a verb or format alone. A multiple-choice case can test judgment, while a large project can still amount to copied procedure.

Use [Alignment map](assets/alignment-map.md) and [Assessment specification](assets/assessment-specification.md). Optional [Structural audit](references/structural-audit.md) checks a declared ID/reference manifest for missing links and unknown references. It cannot establish cognitive alignment, validity, fairness or learning quality.

## Author usable materials

Read [Module authoring](references/module-authoring.md). Produce the scope requested: complete learner instructions, relevant explanations/examples, practice, feedback/answers where appropriate, assessment/rubric and facilitator needs. Do not call a collection of placeholders or topics a delivered lesson. Show material gaps and source/rights dependencies honestly.

Adapt support to the audience and observed difficulty. Offer foundations or alternative paths where a mixed audience needs them; avoid forcing all learners through one assumed prerequisite ladder. Maintain clear links between materials and the authoritative objective/assessment records.

## Review and pilot

Read [Delivery and evaluation](references/delivery-evaluation.md). Review content accuracy, instructions, accessibility, feasibility and assessment evidence. A structural pass is preliminary. A representative learner/facilitator pilot can expose hidden prerequisites and unrealistic timing, but requires actual authorized participants and records; do not invent a pilot or its results.

Use [Review and pilot receipt](assets/review-pilot.md) to distinguish authored, reviewed, locally packaged, platform-previewed and learner-tested states. LMS publishing, enrollment, learner-data processing and external messaging retain their own permissions. [Acceptance briefs](references/acceptance.md) are future tasks. [Design notes](references/design-notes.md) record upstream coverage and tradeoffs.

## Practical professional training

For a workplace skill workshop,coached demonstration or transfer plan,read [Professional practice](references/professional-practice.md). Reuse the outcomes,materials and assessment workflow above,with observed task criteria and authorized learner evidence rather than another duplicate course package. Use [Training session](assets/training-session.md) for delivery and follow-up.

For a staff learning program across roles/cohorts,read [Staff training](references/staff-training.md) and use [Training program](assets/training-program.md). This extends practical training with actual role coverage,delivery ownership and private progress boundaries.

## Build a practical course

## Staff program coverage

Given two role cohorts and a real policy/task change,prepare a program that reuses common material and provides role-specific practice. Acceptance:actual requirement/owner,realistic access/capacity,distinct planned/delivered/completed/assessed states and private progress boundaries. No automatic enrollment,invites,certification or employment judgment.

# Activities and assessment

For each required outcome, identify how learners will practice the actual operation and what evidence can show it. A complete map names the content/input, learner action, support, feedback and assessment. A link in a table does not prove the activity prepares the learner.

## Practice

Use a meaningful task with clear inputs, output and completion criterion. A learner should know what to do without guessing the instructor's intent. Include enough relevant information and tools, then choose scaffolding appropriate to the starting point. A reading can provide necessary input, but a required decision or procedure also needs an opportunity to perform or reason through it.

Vary context when transfer matters. Repeating a demonstrated answer can check attention or recall; it does not alone demonstrate independent application. Provide feedback at a useful point and allow a relevant correction/retry when the objective requires practice. Avoid decorative interactions that consume time without supporting the outcome.

## Assessment demand

Choose evidence from the intended skill, conditions and stakes. A short selected-response case may assess interpretation if the distractors distinguish reasoning. A practical task may require an artifact, trace, explanation or observed process. Do not infer quality solely from the assessment's format or size.

Specify the task, permitted resources, submission, evaluation criteria and feedback. Use observable criterion descriptions rather than excellent/good/poor labels without meaning. Separate content correctness from presentation polish unless presentation is part of the outcome. Make weightings and pass rules explicit when supplied; do not invent institutional grading policy.

Include expected answers or scoring guidance appropriate to the task and protect them from accidental inclusion in the learner-facing version when needed. Accept multiple valid solutions where the domain permits them. Check that question wording and irrelevant language difficulty do not obscure the intended skill.

## Alignment review

Inspect the actual objective, activity instructions, assessment and rubric together. Identify missing practice, missing evidence, mismatched conditions or a rubric that rewards a different skill. Record the reason and a concrete correction. The optional structural helper detects only declared reference/coverage gaps; human/domain review must assess meaning.

Administrative or enrichment activities can be intentionally outside assessed outcomes. Keep them separate from the helper's declared instructional manifest or explain the exception in the course record. Do not force a meaningless objective onto every welcome message to satisfy a machine check.

## Learner evidence

A completion click, satisfaction survey and assessment performance answer different questions. Keep participation, enjoyment, immediate achievement and later task transfer separate. Do not claim training caused a workplace outcome from an uncontrolled before/after observation without discussing other explanations.

# Delivery and evaluation

Define the delivered state: design specification, complete source materials, locally packaged artifact, learning-platform preview, published course or learner-tested offering. These are separate claims. A ZIP that opens is not proof that a learning platform tracks completion or that learners acquired the skill.

## Review

Check domain accuracy, outcomes/practice/assessment meaning, learner instructions, expected resources, accessibility, estimated effort and support. Inspect the actual materials and rubric rather than accepting a filled alignment table. Verify referenced sources and asset rights within the task scope.

For an existing course, compare required changes to the original and preserve approved content/policies. Keep a revision record and validate meaningful links after moving files. Avoid silently replacing unknown instructor dates, grading rules or contact information with plausible fiction.

## Pilot

Plan a small representative trial when it can resolve material uncertainty. Define participant context, permissions, task, data handling, observation method and success criterion. Keep assistance visible: a facilitator explaining every instruction changes what the pilot demonstrates. Do not recruit/contact people or collect learner records without the applicable authorization.

Record observed completion, misunderstandings, time/effort and assessed performance with relevant denominators. Separate designer prediction from learner evidence. A few successful participants can reveal usability issues but do not establish a universal effect size or certify learning quality.

## Target platform

When export/import is requested, inspect the current platform and supported format/version. Packaging standards, navigation and tracking must be tested in the actual authorized environment. Keep credentials out of shared materials. Do not enroll learners, overwrite a live course, start paid integrations or publish to obtain a screenshot.

## Improve

Use evidence to choose the next correction: missing prerequisite, confusing instructions, insufficient practice, bad scoring criterion or a platform fault. Do not lengthen content automatically after every failed item. Keep unresolved issues with a concrete acceptance step and owner rather than converting them into a generic pass.

Report authored/reviewed/piloted/published states separately, including actual commands, participants or platform only when those actions occurred. Preserve private learner responses; a portable settings/template package should not contain them by default.

# Design notes and scope

Independently authored English course-design workflow and resources. Original prompts,code,templates and evidence-tier labels are not redistributed. Reviewed source entrypoints are pinned privately; this is not an exhaustive audit of their complete platform.

# Module authoring

Write for the actual learner and modality. A self-paced module needs sufficient explanation, resources and feedback to proceed independently. A facilitated session needs usable instructions, timing assumptions and facilitator guidance. Do not confuse an instructor's topic outline with learner-ready content.

## Build the learning path

Open with the meaningful task and required starting point. Explain the relevant concept or process in an accessible sequence with examples that match the outcome. Make relationships and transitions clear without repeating the same objective paragraph on every page. Define necessary terminology when it first matters.

Provide a worked or contrasting example when it reveals a non-obvious decision. Verify its correctness and source rights. Distinguish a synthetic example from a real case; do not invent named participants or operational results. Then give the learner a manageable attempt with clear inputs and expected output.

Use headings, lists, tables, diagrams or media where they improve comprehension. Avoid decorative media that competes with the task or requires an unavailable service. Describe assets still needed rather than presenting placeholders as complete. For a technical lesson, ensure code/data examples match the intended runtime and label actual execution evidence.

## Support and feedback

Add hints, error explanations and a route back to the relevant material where useful. Provide an independent transfer opportunity rather than revealing the entire answer before every attempt. Make facilitator-only answers and learner-facing material distinct. An AI-generated explanation still needs substantive subject review when accuracy matters.

For mixed starting points, identify optional foundations and more challenging extensions without making the essential path confusing. Choose length and segmentation around meaningful tasks and learner control, not a universal page/word/time cap. Estimate effort for doing the work as well as consuming the content.

## Usability and access

Use readable structure, meaningful link labels, descriptive alternatives for necessary visuals and usable table headers. Plan captions/transcripts and keyboard interaction for media/platform features. Preserve the instructional purpose when offering an alternative format; an inaccessible drag interaction may need an equivalent reasoning task rather than a static screenshot.

Check language/register and cultural assumptions. Avoid requiring unnecessary personal disclosure for practice. Use fictional cases and synthetic data when the learning objective does not require real records. Follow the institution's actual accessibility and learner-support process; do not fabricate contact details or certification statements.

## Readback

Review the exported or platform-previewed artifact, not only the source text. Confirm links, asset dependencies, answer separation and navigation. A Markdown document can be complete as a design deliverable while LMS interaction/tracking remains untested. State the exact delivered form and missing target acceptance.

# Outcomes and scope

Name the course's practical purpose and audience before selecting content. Use supplied performance examples, task observations, existing assessments or learner work where authorized. Keep evidence and assumptions separate. A stakeholder request for a course is useful context but not proof that instruction solves the underlying problem.

## Define observable outcomes

Write what the learner will do, under which relevant conditions and what acceptable performance looks like. Include constraints only when they matter to the real task. An objective such as knowing a topic needs a more observable interpretation; do not merely swap in a fashionable action verb while leaving the task vague.

Distinguish factual recall, conceptual interpretation, procedural execution and strategic judgment where that distinction changes practice or assessment. A taxonomy can help discussion, but context and actual work determine the demand. Avoid claiming a universal cognitive level from the word analyze, explain or design alone.

Choose stable local objective IDs so activities, assessments and later revisions can refer to the same intended outcome. Keep each outcome meaningful rather than splitting it into many trivial checklist items. Separate required outcomes from optional enrichment, orientation and administrative information.

## Scope and sequencing

Map the essential task dependencies and learner starting point. Some learners benefit from a worked example, some from an initial challenge with targeted support. Treat those as design choices to test, not fixed rules about every novice or expert. Provide a route for learners with different prior knowledge when the task warrants it.

Estimate time for reading/listening, practice, feedback, revision and assessment, not only presentation length. State assumptions about available equipment, internet, language and facilitator support. If the scope exceeds the budget, explain the tradeoff and propose a smaller coherent outcome rather than compressing every activity into an implausible timetable.

## Revision boundary

For an existing course, identify which materials already serve the outcomes and which specific gaps need repair. Preserve stable IDs, valid links, approved policy and useful learner context. Do not overwrite the original course merely because a new template is available. For new work, distinguish a full course from a prototype/sample module in the delivery record.

## Content authority

Identify domain experts and trustworthy references for factual or procedural claims. Do not invent research citations, institutional standards or named policies. Where current law, safety practice, exam specification or technical API is central, use the applicable authoritative current source within the user's permission scope. A course structure can be ready while domain approval remains open.

# Professional practice and training delivery

Start with the actual work outcome and the people who need to perform it. Inspect supplied task standards,current process,tools and examples of performance where authorized. Separate a knowledge/skill gap from missing access,unclear responsibility,broken tooling or conflicting incentives. Training can support a change without resolving every organizational cause by itself.

## Task and audience

Name the task,conditions,permitted tools and acceptable output. Identify consequential decision points and what a learner should do when the situation is outside their authority. Use the current organization/domain procedure rather than inventing a policy or claiming an informal exercise grants professional certification.

Use evidence of prior attempts to choose support. A shared job title does not mean every participant starts at the same point. Avoid fixed assumptions about novice/expert needs or permanent learning styles. Provide a useful route for missing prerequisites while allowing relevant experienced learners to practice the actual challenge.

## Session design

Connect a brief demonstration or worked example to a realistic learner attempt. Explain the important decision and its rationale,then let the learner act in an authorized simulation or disposable environment. Include the likely error/recovery path and an observable output. A slide presentation about a procedure is different from demonstrated ability to perform it.

Use the course alignment map and assessment specification for meaningful criteria. A roleplay or practical task needs clear instructions,feedback and a fair way to observe the intended skill. Separate domain correctness from presentation style unless style is itself the target. Do not fabricate institutional pass thresholds or certification rules.

## Facilitation

Make the task and available support clear. Invite questions and adapt from actual difficulty. Preserve learner turns;do not perform every step for them and then mark the task mastered. In a group,avoid exposing personal performance data unnecessarily. Use synthetic cases when real customer,employee or operational records are not required.

A real workshop,participant contact or production task requires applicable authorization and access. A prepared session plan is not evidence that delivery occurred. Keep proposed demonstrations and observed demonstrations distinct. Do not activate a service,send a message or mutate live business data merely to demonstrate a skill.

## Transfer and evaluation

Plan a fresh relevant task or later work sample to check transfer when appropriate and permitted. Record conditions and assistance. Attendance,satisfaction,immediate practice and workplace results answer different questions;do not claim one proves another. A business metric can change for several reasons besides training.

Use minimal authorized notes and the established owner process for feedback. Do not turn a tutoring observation into an employee performance judgment or store private responses in a portable template pack. Deliver session materials,actual evidence if any,remaining domain approval and the precise next practice/target check.

This package is written in English and uses the open Agent Skills folder format. Its core workflow is independent of the model provider.

- Codex: place the package in the workspace or user `.agents/skills/` directory supported by the installed version, or load its SKILL.md explicitly.
- Claude Code: use the supported `.claude/skills/` workspace/user directory, or load SKILL.md explicitly. Other Claude surfaces may accept an uploaded skill archive instead.
